transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-27 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Samira Khan (Equinox Head of Platform), Jonas Reed (Equinox SRE), Priya Patel (Equinox Security), Alex Moreno (Product)

Summary:
Quick intake to map Equinox's reliability targets and design a staged fault-injection stress test for fallback policies across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Main concerns: cascade failures during region outage, cold-start latency for fallback variants, KV cache consistency during steering, and compliance constraints for private deployment.

00:00 - Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. can you hear me ok?
00:05 - Samira (Equinox): yep, loud and clear. thanks for setting this up. we've got about 45 minutes.
00:12 - Maya: great, we wanted to walk through your goals for a stress test — like what you mean by "fallback" and what success looks like. diego and i will take notes and propose next steps.
00:25 - Jonas: our context — we run chat assistants for clinical intake, high p99 SLA expectation. real time-ish. when a region gets noisy we need automated fallbacks without losing session context.
00:36 - Diego (Redwood): mm-hmm, ok. when you say "session context" is that full KV cache per user or tokenized prompts persisted in your app layer?
00:44 - Jonas: it's a combo. we keep short-term context in our app, but we rely on model KV cache for decoder speed. there's a concern about priming and double-prime when traffic switches regions.
00:55 - Priya (Security): and from security, if we route to another region we need KMS key wrapping policies honored, audit logs, and data residency rules — we can't send PII outside EMEA for certain endpoints.
01:08 - Maya: understood. so we should map routing policy tiers: 1) local-region hosted (preferred), 2) remote-region hosted fallback, 3) dedicated pool in same region, 4) private (on-prem) as last resort. is that roughly the idea?
01:20 - Samira: yes, except we might swap 2/3 depending on latency. cost is secondary; safety and correctness first.
01:28 - Diego: a quick note — Redwood supports prefix/KV cache warming and automatic prefix caching. in a failover we can attempt to transfer KV or rely on prompt-level rehydration. there's tradeoffs: restoring KV is faster but fragile across model variants.
01:44 - Jonas: i've seen issues where fallback model answers are inconsistent because the variant was quantized differently. how do you handle model variant mismatch?
01:52 - Diego: good question — runtime has model compatibility layers. for production we recommend model variants with compatible tokenization and mesh rules. but for the stress test we should exercise a scenario where primary is high-precision (fp16/quant) and fallback is a smaller quantized variant to see behavioral drift.
02:10 - Alex (Product): on the stress test shape — we want to simulate a regional outage and also a partial degradation where p95 doubles. can Redwood do staged injection like 5m outage, 30m degraded, then full failover?
02:22 - Maya: yes, we can coordinate a staged test. typical template: baseline 20m, degrade 30m with introduced delays and dropped requests, then region cutover for 10-15m. we'll capture token-level latencies and error traces.
02:34 - Samira: how about traffic steering — do you support weighted split per route so we can test canary + rapid rollback?
02:41 - Diego: yes, traffic split, canary, and circuit-breakers. we also have automatic fallback policy where if a route exceeds error threshold we steer to fallback variants. you can tune thresholds.
02:51 - Priya: auditability: during the test we need detailed logs for compliance review — SAML assertions, KMS key IDs per call, and an immutable audit trail.
02:59 - Maya: we can provide audit logs and a SOC 2 summary. for private deployments we can integrate with your HSM. we'll attach security docs.
03:08 - Jonas: one more, sticky sessions — if we route a user mid-conversation to fallback, will their session be preserved? how do you keep the KV cache tied?
03:17 - Diego: if the fallback is in same model family and we warm caches, session continuity is good. otherwise we create a rehydration prompt that includes last N turns; that's more tokens but preserves semantics. for the stress test we'll measure both paths.

03:30 - [Agenda check — 2 more topics: failure modes and acceptance criteria]
03:36 - Maya: let's catalogue failure modes you care about. Jonas?
03:40 - Jonas: regional outage, noisy neighbors causing queueing, private-network partition (VPC peering flap), and a cascading model overload where latency spikes cause client retries.
03:51 - Diego: for noisy neighbors we can exercise autoscaling and see time to recover; for VPC peering we'll simulate connectivity loss and ensure TLS/KMS handshakes fail gracefully.
04:04 - Samira: we need SLO numbers: p95 under 250ms token latency for baseline; p99 under 1s in steady state. anything above 2s triggers failover. are those numbers reasonable to plan against?
04:17 - Maya: reasonable. we'll instrument the test to flag p95/p99 and to simulate threshold-driven failover. we'll also look at error budget burn.
04:25 - Priya: risk of data exfil: during region failover logs might be replicated to another region, we need to confirm log redaction.
04:33 - Diego: we'll show how log retention and cross-region replication are configurable; also can redact PII fields before export.

04:45 - [10m mark — Maya shares a link]
04:46 - Maya: sharing: drive.redwood.com/fallback-benchmarks.xlsx (short link) — it's the template we'll populate.
04:52 - Alex: got it, we'll drop our traffic profile doc there.
04:56 - Samira: curious about cost delta for dedicated vs hosted during the test — a rough multiplier is fine.
05:02 - Maya: hosted is usage-based; dedicated has reserved GPU pools. for high SLOs dedicated reduces tail variance but costs more. we'll include a cost/latency matrix in the follow up.
05:12 - Jonas: what about a hybrid — keep primary hosted but burst to dedicated when error budget is low?
05:18 - Diego: that's supported via smart routing policies: policy can route to a capacity tier when latency or errors exceed thresholds. we can configure autoscale + burst.

05:30 - [12m mark — deeper technical question]
05:32 - Jonas: how do you ensure model cache integrity when models auto-roll? if a model is rolled mid-test can it break the KV format?
05:40 - Diego: we recommend pinning model versions for tests. Redwood supports rollouts but rolling during a stress test is risky. KV cache formats are tied to model tokenizer and architecture — we flag incompatible rollouts.
05:52 - Samira: ok, we'll pin versions for the pilot.

06:00 - Maya: let's define acceptance criteria for the staged stress test. proposed: 1) failover triggers within 30s of threshold breach, 2) session continuity (rehydration or cache transfer) for 90% of test sessions, 3) no PII forwarded outside region-excluded endpoints, 4) final p99 below 1.5s for fallback path.
06:20 - Priya: we need attestations for point 3 from Redwood security team.
06:24 - Maya: yes, we'll include security attestation and config docs.

06:30 - [18m mark — objections and clarifications]
06:32 - Alex: our legal asks: can you support an SLA addendum for the pilot period?
06:36 - Maya: for pilots we typically provide operational guardrails but SLA addendum is a sales contract conversation — i'll loop in sales ops.
06:43 - Samira: timeline — we'd like pilot within 2-3 weeks. is that realistic?
06:47 - Maya: yes, if we get telemetry and traffic profile this week we can schedule a pilot kickoff in two weeks.

07:00 - [22m mark — Diego describes test harness]
07:02 - Diego: test harness will replay traffic at desired RPS, allow fault injection (latency, dropped connections, DNS blackhole), and swap routing policies. we'll run parallel runs for hosted/dedicated/private if you want.
07:15 - Jonas: for private we have a gov-on-prem cluster — can the harness run from our network?
07:21 - Diego: yes, we can run remote agents inside your VPC; for on-prem there's an installer that collects only metrics and controls routing via secure channels.
07:32 - Priya: encryption in transit for control plane?
07:35 - Diego: yes, mutual TLS; for private we can also integrate with your HSM and never persist keys on Redwood-managed hosts.

07:45 - Samira: can we also run a chaos test where routing decisions oscillate to validate circuit-breakers?
07:51 - Diego: absolutely. we can script oscillations and measure thrashing and convergence times.

08:02 - [28m mark — notes on metrics]
08:04 - Maya: metrics we'll collect: token-level latency, request-level latency, error rates, CPU/GPU utilization, cache hit rates, and model output quality degradation metrics (BLEU-ish for our domain).
08:15 - Alex: do you support custom evals for quality regressions? we have prompt sets we use for acceptance tests.
08:20 - Diego: yes — Redwood Optimize can run quality monitors against prompt sets; we'll include that.

08:30 - [33m mark — cost discussion and billing]
08:32 - Maya: we'll prepare an estimated cost delta spreadsheet for hosting patterns. remember dedicated is commit-based; hosted is on-demand. during the pilot costs are usually covered under an evaluation credit or time-limited pilot agreement.
08:47 - Samira: perfect. that helps procurement.

08:52 - [40m mark — wrap-up of technical agreements]
08:53 - Maya: quick recap: 1) Equinox will share traffic profile, telemetry, and prompt/test set by 2026-08-31. 2) Redwood (Maya/Diego) will provide benchmark template, initial routing policies, security docs, and pilot schedule by 2026-09-01. 3) Plan a pilot kickoff week of 2026-09-14 (tentative).
09:14 - Jonas: noted. one more nit — how are retries handled at client side? we need idempotency keys to avoid duplicate side effects.
09:21 - Diego: we recommend idempotency tokens and also support server-side dedupe for some endpoints. we'll document best practices.

09:30 - Priya: last question: do you have previous case studies for regional failover in regulated environments?
09:34 - Maya: yes, we'll share a redacted case study and an SOC 2 summary; link will be in the follow-up.

09:40 - [closing minutes]
09:41 - Maya: thanks all — we'll send the follow-up with links and the test plan. can i confirm Samira will own the telemetry drop?
09:47 - Samira: yes, i'll own it.
09:50 - Maya: perfect. Diego and i will prep config and a short runbook. thanks, bye.
09:55 - Alex: thanks everyone. bye.

Notes on transcription: some product names were misheard (K V cash vs KV cache), and acronyms like SAML/SOC sometimes transcribed as "Sam L" or "sock two". speaker labels pulled from calendar might be slightly off.
